name: INT. MANHATTAN OFFICE - NIGHT
description: Jess turns down Christmas; the siren answers for her.

elements.text: Stage 1: She refuses, then she has to come home
Jess turns down Christmas; the siren answers for her.
Black.
Jess at her desk at nine at night. Her window faces a brick airshaft lit by someone else's fluorescent light.
(still typing, apologizing)
Mom, I'm sorry. I can't come home for Christmas this year. Work is crazy.
(on the phone; warm, unhurried, a woman who has never once raised her voice to win)
Oh, honey. I understand.

fountainNotes: id=01d to=JESS fx=phone emo=affectionate:2 act=disarm pace=slow

elements.text: A siren rises on Linda's end of the line only.
(typing stops)
Mom? Is that a siren?
(pleasant, as if it's the mailman)
Don't worry, sweetheart. I think it's for me.
The siren bends down in pitch and becomes a single piano note.
She promises work: two days.
Sleet in the headlights. Jess grips the wheel, still in her office clothes.
Her boss is a faint, impatient murmur over the car speaker.
(hiding the panic)
My mom's in the hospital. Two days. I'll be back in two days, I promise.
I don't really fit here anymore. Everyone still thinks I'm seventeen.

direction.say: Confiding, slightly self-conscious. A small rueful smile on seventeen.

extras.phoneConversation: Only Jess is heard; an undefined romantic possibility in New York. Not an established partner.

elements.text: I know, but things will be better in the new year, when this project finishes. And yes, I'll be there for the New Year's Eve party.

direction.say: Reassuring the person on the phone, trying to convince herself too. Warm, tired, conversational.

extras.phoneConversation: Only Jess is heard; an undefined romantic possibility in New York. Not an established partner.

name: INT./EXT. HOSTETTER HOUSE, ANNVILLE - NIGHT
description: She comes home. The injury is real, small and funny.

elements.text: She comes home. The injury is real, small and funny.
Main Street, lights strung across it.
ANNVILLE, PENNSYLVANIA
In the yard, an inflatable snowman lies half-deflated beside a fallen ladder.
Linda beams from a teal recliner, her white leg cast propped on a footstool. A sparse, undecorated Christmas tree stands behind her. Jess comes in, coat on, bag in hand.
(lighting up, completely casual)
You came home!
(breathless, four hours of driving in her voice)
Mom, you were in an ambulance!
(reasonable)
It's just a sprain. The neighbors called an ambulance.

direction.say: Warm, matter-of-fact reassurance to her worried daughter. Gentle falling cadence. No punchline.

extras.previousText: It's a sprained ankle, sweetheart. They offered.

elements.text: Jess kneels beside Linda's cast. Linda's hand goes to her cheek.
Stage 2: She tries to leave and gets stuck

name: EXT. TURKEY HILL CHARGING AREA - DAWN
description: A charging stop becomes a collision: distracted by work, Jess backs into a snowplow.

value.heading: EXT. TURKEY HILL CHARGING AREA - DAWN

elements.text: She leaves on schedule. The plow stops her.
Low battery. Jess pulls into Turkey Hill and spots the chargers. Her roller bag is in the back seat. A snowplow is parked behind the charging spaces.

direction.note: Keep store signage soft-focus unless cleared.

fountainNotes: id=04a shot=LS img=turkey-hill-dawn sfx=door.store-chime mus=theme:stop,store-carol:in note="Keep store signage soft-focus unless cleared."

elements.text: On a work call, Jess reverses toward a charger. Her attention is on the phone, not the snowplow behind her.
(on the phone, brisk, already gone in her head)
I'm charging now. Send me the revisions. I'll look at them on the way.

direction.say: Distracted work call, brisk and conversational.

extras.previousText: She's fine. I'll be back in the office by noon--

elements.text: Crunch. Her rear wheel catches the snowplow blade. Jess stops; the car is damaged.
One full second of nothing but the store carol.
Dot, seventies, blaze-orange cap, coffee in hand by the door. Unmoved.
(appraising, not angry)
I'll call you back.

direction.say: Quietly stunned after a bump. A little embarrassed.

name: EXT./INT. KREIDER’S AUTO - DAY
description: The mechanic is her high-school crush. He remembers her; she pretends not to remember him.

elements.text: The mechanic is her high-school crush. He remembers her; she pretends not to remember him.
Wide exterior of Kreider’s Auto. Snow borders the service bays; Jess’s car waits by the open bay. Cut inside to Ben.

fountainNotes: id=05a shot=LS img=garage-boots sfx=tool.impact-wrench mus=store-carol:out,comedy:in amb=shop-radio:in,space-heater:in

elements.text: The creeper rolls out.
(sees her; tiny pause)
Please tell me you’re open.

direction.say: Hopeful, slightly embarrassed, speaking to the mechanic in the doorway.

fountainNotes: id=05c to=JESS emo=interested:2,amused:1 act=greet pace=slow pre=0.4

elements.text: Jess, in a city coat too thin for the weather.
(too bright)
For you, or the car?

direction.say: Confident, warm, gently teasing. A small smile, not a big punchline.

elements.text: Ben wipes his hands. Not smiling yet.
(lets it sit a beat; dry)
(caught)

name: INT. KREIDER'S AUTO / JESS'S CHILDHOOD BEDROOM - DAY

value.heading: INT. KREIDER'S AUTO / JESS'S CHILDHOOD BEDROOM - DAY

elements.text: The forced stay.
Ben points out a bent rear suspension arm beside the wheel.
The plow bent your rear suspension. You can’t drive it like this.

direction.say: Plain, clear explanation. Calm competent mechanic, not dramatic.

extras.previousText: The sensor's cracked. The part has to come from the factory.

elements.text: (urgent)
How long?
The part gets here December twenty-ninth.

direction.say: Matter-of-fact, reassuring. Normal conversation, not a punchline.

elements.text: The twenty-ninth? I promised I'd be back for New Year's Eve.

direction.say: Brief surprise, then worried about the promise she made. Natural conversational emphasis.

elements.text: (beat, gently)
Well, you’re not going anywhere today.

direction.say: Warm, low male voice. Matter-of-fact but gently amused, not parental or patronizing.

elements.text: Wait. Do I know you?

direction.say: Sudden recognition. Curious and warm, a small pause after Wait.

elements.text: Ben Kreider. You borrowed my truck for the homecoming parade.

direction.say: Relaxed, grounded confidence. A small amused smile, not eager or awkward.

extras.previousText: Ben Kreider. We had chemistry together. You sat right behind me.

elements.text: Ben. Of course. Hi.
The roller bag back on Jess's childhood bed, under a high-school pennant.

name: INT. KREIDER'S AUTO - DAYS LATER (SERIES OF SHOTS)
description: Days pass. She still asks, out of habit.

value.heading: INT. KREIDER'S AUTO - DAYS LATER (SERIES OF SHOTS)

elements.text: Days pass. She still asks, out of habit.
The same garage doorway three times. Her coat changes, the snow deepens, one coffee becomes two.

fountainNotes: id=07a shot=MS(JESS) img=doorway-1,doorway-2,doorway-3 mus=comedy:sting note="One celesta note per still."

elements.text: (leaning in the doorway, by rote)
Any news on the part?
(doesn't look up)
Not yet.
Stage 3: She chooses to stay

name: EXT. FARM LANE, EDGE OF TOWN - SUNSET
description: The turn. Work calls; she lets it go.

value.heading: EXT. FARM LANE, EDGE OF TOWN - SUNSET

elements.text: The turn. Work calls; she lets it go.
Ben's truck faces a wide field and the low sun. Two silhouettes, a bench seat of space between them.

direction.note: Music drops to one held string note.

fountainNotes: id=08a shot=TWO(BEN,JESS,size=MS) move=push-in/slow img=truck-rear-window mus=theme:drop amb=truck-idle:in,heater-fan:in,crows-distant:in note="Music drops to one held string note."

elements.text: Jess in profile, lit orange. A few flakes drift.
(quiet but voiced, not whispered; half a laugh at herself)
In the city, I never get to see the sun go down. It's just gone by four o'clock.

fountainNotes: id=08c to=BEN emo=wistful:2,amused:1 act=confide vol=soft pace=slow

elements.text: Her phone lights up on the dash: WORK. It buzzes. Her hand turns it face-down. The buzzing stops.
Ben turns the key. The engine stops. Wind, and the engine block ticking.
(low, simple)
Stay a while. It's worth the wait.

fountainNotes: id=08f to=JESS emo=affectionate:2 act=invite vol=soft pace=slow pre=1.0

elements.text: The theme returns, four notes. The fifth is held back.

name: INT. KREIDER'S AUTO, OFFICE - DAY
description: The overheard remark. It hurts because she was starting to stay.

elements.text: The overheard remark. It hurts because she was starting to stay.
Jess in the office doorway with a cardboard tray of two coffees.
(to his uncle, matter-of-fact)
Don't get attached. She'll be gone the minute that car is fixed.
The cardboard tray crunches in her hand.
(very level)
Is that really what you think of me?
Ben turns around, caught.
(half a second too late)
Jess, wait. That's not what I meant.
The convention, promised and withheld.
Crowd, breath steam, kids on shoulders. The tree is still dark.
Jess alone in the crowd, scanning.
Ben's truck parked at the edge of the square, empty.
(mic too close, civic cheer)
Okay, folks! Let's light this tree!
Five! Four! Three! Two--

fountainNotes: id=10e emo=excited:3 vol=x-loud pace=medium end=cutoff mus=tannenbaum:out,theme:swell

elements.text: SMASH CUT TO:
Total silence, longer than is comfortable.
A field at the last edge of sunset, the horizon low in the frame.

direction.note: One piano chord on the theme's fourth note, held.

elements.text: CHRISTMAS, FACING WEST

name: INT. HOSTETTER HOUSE - NIGHT
description: The button: the car has been ready for days, and she still hasn't left.

elements.text: The button: the car has been ready for days, and she still hasn't left.
Linda in the recliner, the landline cord around one finger, eating pie straight from the tin.
(low, conspiratorial, delighted)
Dot, her car's been ready since Tuesday.

fountainNotes: id=13b to=DOT emo=mischievous:2 act=confide vol=soft pace=medium

elements.text: (beat)
And she still hasn't left.

fountainNotes: id=13c to=DOT emo=mischievous:3,pleased:2 act=reveal vol=soft pace=slow pre=0.6

name: LIGHTS
description: The lighting we were denied, and the theme's fifth note.

elements.text: The lighting we were denied, and the theme's fifth note.
The heavy clunk of the tree lights switching on. The crowd goes "Ohhh!" and cheers. Sleigh bells.
Black blooms into warm, out-of-focus tree lights. We never see the tree or the couple.
COMING THIS CHRISTMAS
